newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollars gain on Greenspan, upside capped.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollars gain on Greenspan, upside capped.

text.p: Three-month U.S. interest rate futures traded on SIMEX ended sharply higher on Friday on the back of comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
But dealers said further rises would be limited and Eurodollar futures could even come off again as players had basically reacted in a knee-jerk fashion to a speech that contained little new.
"The substance of his statements reflects nothing more than what he's said before so the market could go lower," a trader with a European futures house said.

Greenspan said in a speech late Thursday night that he expected economic growth to slow later this year and next, but added that the central bank would need to act if that did not prove to be the case.
"Should the expected slowing in the growth of demand fail to materialise, we would need to address any emerging pressures in product and credit markets," he said.
The most active December Eurodollar contract surged over 10 ticks to a high of 93.725 as players interpreted the comments to mean the Fed might hold back on further rate hikes for now.
The Fed had been widely expected to hike rates again at its policy-making meeting on May 20 after it raised short-term interest rates for the first time in two years in March.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.705 against their IMM close at 93.625 on hectic volume of 45,290 lots. It is expected to face resistance at 93.750 while support is seen at 93.640.
September finished at 93.910 against 93.845 on 27,340 lots.
Japanese interest rate and bond futures also had a volatile session, firming initially on vague rumours another Japanese insurance company was in trouble, dealers said.
But the market remained under pressure for most of the day, partly on follow-through sales after recent declines, and as fears of an impending Japanese interest rate hike gained ground.
A report in a Japanese financial daily speculating on whether the Bank of Japan (BOJ) might raise rates as early as July added to the nervousness, dealers said.
The lead December Euroyen contract stood at 98.85 at 1110 GMT after falling to a low of 98.82 against an IMM close at 98.89. Volume was an active 25,360 lots.

"This market will tend to be supported on dips until there is a clear indication that the BOJ is going to do something," the trader said, adding that most Japanese official rhetoric indicated the economic recovery was not yet self-sustaining.
Dealers said a break of the 98.81 support could expose December Euroyen to a steep drop to around 98.73.
June JGBs ended at 123.27 against their previous 123.86 after touching a low of 122.55. Support is seen at 122.35/40.
